answer: Each epoch the registry auctions fixed entry slots, so an identity must be bought, not minted free. Winners pay the clearing price, lock it twenty epochs, and gain a non-transferable ivory certificate tied to their work. The fable of free entry dies here: the k-th fake still pays its own bid, so 1,000 fakes lock 50,000 credit for twenty epochs, while one honest agent pays a single 50-credit bid and earns it back. Bid histories are mirrored in public, so bids moving together expose one buyer behind many masks, and rented slots void on first use.
